A year later, a Thai doctor sees every vaccine he has received in his life, and no record is copied across the border. This guide is that story, the VaxLink guided walkthrough, put in writing as a digital adaptation kit (DAK, L2) of the WHO SMART Guidelines and a FHIR implementation guide (L3). [23] Thailand and the Lao PDR never connect to each other. Both rely on the WHO GDHCN. Thailand publishes the key with which it signs the certificates, and the Lao PDR caches the trust list, so that its clinics can verify a Thai card without signal. A year later, the same trust list allows a Thai clinic to verify the Lao VHL. Data cross the border in only two ways: as a signed QR card that the family carries, or as a link that the family decides to share. [126] Policy (J2a): Keep a clear line between what families report and what has been verified, and do not grant trust too early.
[127] Policy (J2b): Newborns can be registered at home, offline, before civil registration or a national identity document exists.
[128] Policy (J3a): Trust is decentralized: a Lao clinic verifies a Thai signature by itself, without contacting Thailand.

[17] J1, Cross-border birth and initial vaccination. In Country A (XXR, the country of birth), the provincial hospital administers to a newborn who is not a national of that country the birth doses of Hep B and BCG and issues one signed DVC per dose (DVCMinPreQual in subclaim -6) as a paper QR, without needing a national identity number (the example in section 12, QR Code Generation, of the WHO guide is one of these pairs). The hospital's system is the Issuer (Issuer, SMART Trust) and the HCERT part of the VHL Sharer (VHL Sharer); the private key stays with whoever holds custody of it (two-phase signing, <a0>STT-ISS-004</a0>, <a1>STT-COS-006</a1>). That XXR's DSC, under its CSCA, appears on the GDHCN trust list is a PRECONDITION of issuance, stated below, not a step. The caregiver is the Holder (Holder, SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw) and the VHL Holder (VHL Holder, IHE ITI VHL).
[18] J2 Detect and refer an unregistered infant in Country B
[19] J2, Return to the country, discovery and referral by the community health worker (CHW). Back in Country B (the country of residence, XXH), where the family resides, the community health worker finds, during a home visit, a foreign-born infant who is not on the household roster. Offline, the CHW app adds the infant to the household (a FHIR Group resource, by means of a structured data capture form), reads the foreign DVCs without verifying them (read without verification, <a0>STT-VER-011</a0>: the triage read stops before the trust lookup and marks each field as unverified), saves the doses as reported by the family, not verified (Immunization.primarySource false), and refers the infant to the clinic for verification. Everything is queued on the phone and syncs the next time there is signal. The CHW app is a Receiver (Receiver, SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw) that deliberately stops before trust verification; the caregiver provides the VDHC as Holder (smart-trust-phw requirement provide-a-vhl-to-a-receiver).
[20] J3 Verify, import and schedule at the country-of-residence clinic
[21] J3, Verification at the clinic and schedule generation, in Country B. The clinic's electronic health record (Receiver in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw, VHL Receiver side in IHE ITI VHL) keeps a copy of the GDHCN trust list, which the trust anchor (Trust Network Anchor; IHE Trust Anchor) distributes and which Country B, a Trust Network Participant (Trust Network Participant), retrieves (retrieve-pki-material of smart-trust-phw). Loading the DID documents is a PRECONDITION of this visit, not a step of it: the clinic may be offline the whole time, so the list it verifies with is the one it last updated, roughly every week, when the CHW visits the base clinic or the district health office. It verifies each foreign DVC in the order of <a0>STT-VER-001</a0> with the DID document of XXR's DSC, imports the verified doses with their provenance, adds the national schedule code next to each foreign vaccine code (ConceptMap; the nurse decides on any unmapped product) and evaluates the national schedule, which determines that the 6-week doses are due and schedules them.
[22] J4.0 Issue the family's records as VHLs on a single phone
[23] J4.0, Family trip abroad, "One family, one phone". Before travelling, the caregiver who has the family's only shared phone requests from Country B's national portal the records of each family member, choosing for each one an access code that the family can say aloud and an expiry date (for example, 14 days); the portal records that choice as the holder's consent to share (FHIR Consent, IHE Privacy Consent on FHIR). The portal, which is VHL Sharer (VHL Sharer, IHE ITI VHL) and Issuer (Issuer, SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw), issues an access-code-protected verifiable health link (VHL) for each member: the documents (IPS, DVC) encrypted as JWE (<a0>STT-VHL-007</a0>) behind an ITI-YY5 manifest, and the link in the SMART Health Links payload format in key 5 of the HCERT (<a1>STT-VHL-001</a1>, <a2>STT-VHL-002</a2>), signed with Country B's DSC. The shared phone keeps the QRs for the caregiver, the VHL Holder. The records remain hosted in Country B: the QR only contains a pointer and a key.
[24] J4.1 Read a family member's records at the point of care abroad
[25] J4.1. Abroad, a child of the family needs care. The caregiver, VHL Holder (VHL Holder, IHE ITI VHL; Holder in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw, requirement provide-a-vhl-to-a-receiver), opens their QR on the family phone and says the passcode. The hospital's system, a VHL Receiver (VHL Receiver; Receiver in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw), verifies the HCERT against the GDHCN trust list, requests the manifest via ITI-YY5 with an HTTP Message Signature (<a0>STT-VHL-005</a0>, <a1>STT-VHL-006</a1>, <a2>STT-VHL-008</a2>) and decrypts the documents (<a3>STT-VHL-007</a3>). Country B's portal checks the passcode, returns the manifest and logs each request, granted or denied, as an AuditEvent in the country of residence (IHE BALP). If the HCERT does not verify, there is no digital verification: the VHL is not followed and the records are treated as paper. As in J3, loading the DID documents is a PRECONDITION of this visit, not a step of it: the hospital verifies with its cached copy of the trust list and needs no connection to do so. It updates that cache every night or every hour, whereas an offline site, such as the J3 clinic, updates it roughly every week.
